name: manage_asset
description:
PREFERRED tool for all asset operations — use this instead of Python AssetDiscoveryService calls. Manages Unreal Engine assets: search by name/type, find by exact path, list by folder, open in editor, save, save_all, duplicate, move, delete, or import an image file from disk. 

IMPORTING FROM DISK: action='import' brings an image file on disk into the Content Browser as a Texture2D. Use this instead of Python unreal.AssetTools import_asset_tasks / ImportAssets — those pump the task graph and crash the editor when called from a tool. Supported formats: png, jpg, jpeg, bmp, tga, dds, exr, hdr, tiff, tif, psd, pcx.
  Import an image      : action='import', source_file_path='C:/Images/rocks.jpg', destination_path='/Game/UI/Textures', asset_name='T_Rocks'


WORKFLOW: Always search/find FIRST to confirm the exact path before editing.
  User says 'BP_Player' -> manage_asset(action='search', search_term='BP_Player', asset_type='Blueprint')
  Never guess paths. Use the object_path from results as asset_path in subsequent calls.

COMMON PATTERNS:
  Find by partial name : action='search', search_term='BP_Enemy', asset_type='Blueprint'
  Confirm exact path   : action='find',   asset_path='/Game/AI/ST_Cube'
  List folder contents : action='list',   path='/Game/AI'
  Open in editor       : action='open',   asset_path='/Game/AI/ST_Cube'
  Save after edits     : action='save',   asset_path='/Game/AI/ST_Cube'
  Save all dirty       : action='save_all'
  Duplicate asset      : action='duplicate', source_path='...', destination_path='...'  (for true copies only)
  Move or rename asset : action='move', source_path='...', destination_path='...'  (preserves references)
  Delete (guarded)     : action='delete', asset_path='...'  (blocked if referenced; use skip_reference_check=true to override)

Never emulate a move by duplicating then deleting the original. That creates a different asset and can break references.
  Per-action docs      : action='help', help_action='search'

All paths use Content Browser format: /Game/..., /Engine/..., or /PluginName/...
Search covers ALL content roots (Game, Engine, Plugins) automatically.

asset_path.description: Content Browser path to a single asset (e.g. /Game/Blueprints/BP_Player). Required for: find, open, save, delete.

search_term.description: Partial name to match against asset names (case-insensitive). Used with action='search'.

asset_type.description: Asset class filter: Blueprint, StaticMesh, Texture2D, Material, AnimSequence, etc. Optional for: search, list.

path.description: Content Browser folder path to list recursively (e.g. /Game/AI). Used with action='list'.

source_path.description: Source asset path for action='duplicate' or action='move'.

destination_path.description: Destination asset path for action='duplicate' or action='move'.

skip_reference_check.description: If true, skip the reference check before delete (default false). Used with action='delete'.

source_file_path.description: Absolute path to an image file on disk (e.g. C:/Images/rocks.jpg). Required for action='import'.

asset_name.description: Optional asset name for action='import'. If omitted, derived from the source file name.

help_action.description: Specific action name to get detailed help for. Used with action='help'.

name: run_automation_tests
description:
Run the engine's Automation Tests (unit, functional, Revvy's own plugin tests) inside this editor and read per-test pass/fail back as structured JSON. THE way to verify editor-side changes actually work.

The run is ASYNCHRONOUS so the editor never freezes and latent tests get real frames: action='run' returns immediately with status='running'. Poll action='status' until status='idle', then read action='last_result'.

ACTIONS:
  list         : enumerate registered tests (filter substring, e.g. filter='Revvy.').
  run          : start tests matching the REQUIRED 'filter'. Returns queued/skipped counts.
  status       : [completed/total], current test, elapsed seconds. 'idle' means finished.
  last_result  : per-test {state: passed|failed|skipped|timeout, duration, errors[], warnings[]}.
  cancel       : stop after the current test; partial results are kept.
  help         : full parameter and result-shape documentation.

TYPICAL LOOP:
  1. edit code / assets
  2. action='list', filter='Revvy.'   (discover)
  3. action='run', filter='Revvy.'
  4. action='status'  (repeat until idle)
  5. action='last_result'  -> fix failures -> back to 3

Tests run IN-PROCESS: they may create transient objects or open their own PIE session and are expected to clean up. Non-editor-context and RequiresUser tests are skipped by default.

action.description: Operation: list, run, status, last_result, cancel, help

filter.description: [list/run] Case-insensitive substring matched against the full test path and display name. REQUIRED for run

max_tests.description: [run] Refuse to start when the filter matches more than this many tests (default 50, max 500)

include_non_editor_context.description: [run] Also run tests not flagged for editor context (default false - they are recorded as skipped)

timeout_seconds_per_test.description: [run] Abort the run when a single test exceeds this (default 120, range 5-1800)

timeout_seconds.description: [run] Abort the whole run after this many seconds (default 900, range 30-7200)

name: read_blueprint
description: Read the structure of a Blueprint asset: parent class, components (with attachment parents), variables, functions and event dispatchers. Read-only - never modifies, compiles or saves the asset. Takes an asset path such as /Game/Player/BP_Player.

blueprint_path.description: Asset path of the Blueprint, e.g. /Game/Player/BP_Player

name: get_blueprint_derived_classes
description: List Blueprint assets that derive from a native C++ class (directly or through Blueprint parents). Answers from the Asset Registry without loading assets. Read-only. Accepts the class name with or without its U/A prefix, e.g. 'UDSCurrencyDisplayWidget' or 'DSCurrencyDisplayWidget'.

native_class_name.description: Native C++ class name, prefixed or bare

name: build_project
description:
Compile this project's C++ with UnrealBuildTool and read the errors back as structured JSON. Use this to verify your own C++ edits before claiming they work.

The build is ASYNCHRONOUS so the editor never freezes: action='compile' returns immediately with status='running'. Poll action='status' until status='idle', then read action='last_result'.

ACTIONS:
  compile      : start a build of the editor target (auto-detected). Returns build_id + log_path.
  status       : elapsed time, [completed/total] UBT actions, errors so far. 'idle' means it finished.
  last_result  : structured diagnostics of the last finished build. Never rebuilds.
  cancel       : terminate the running build; partial diagnostics are kept.
  help         : full parameter and result-shape documentation.

Each diagnostic is {severity, file, line, column, code, message, raw_snippet, fix_hint}, where fix_hint is a heuristic for common UE mistakes (C2065 -> missing #include, LNK2019 -> module missing from Build.cs, C4996 -> the suggested replacement API). Counts and an overall build_succeeded flag come back alongside.

TYPICAL LOOP:
  1. edit C++
  2. action='compile'
  3. action='status'  (repeat; a cold build takes minutes)
  4. action='last_result'  -> fix the reported errors -> back to 2

Writes Binaries/ and Intermediate/ only; no asset or content is modified. Full output is written to Saved/Revvy/Build/.

action.description: Operation: compile, status, last_result, cancel, help

target.description: [compile] Build target name. Default: editor target auto-detected from <Project>/Source/*.Target.cs (e.g. 'LyraEditor')

platform.description: [compile] Target platform. Default: the host platform (Win64/Mac/Linux)

configuration.description: [compile] Debug, DebugGame, Development, Shipping or Test. Default Development

hot_reload.description: [compile] Default true: let UBT detect the running editor and link a versioned hot-reload DLL. false adds -NoHotReloadFromIDE and may fail with LNK1168 while the editor is open

timeout_seconds.description: [compile] Kill the build after this many seconds (default 900, range 30-7200)

extra_args.description: [compile] Extra arguments appended verbatim to the UnrealBuildTool command line

name: manage_checkpoints
description:
Browse and restore the automatic pre-save snapshots Revvy keeps of every asset file a Revvy tool overwrites - the durable safety net BEHIND editor undo. When a tool saves over an existing file under Content/, the previous on-disk version is copied to Saved/Revvy/Checkpoints first, automatically.

ACTIONS:
  list     : checkpoints newest first ({id, timestamp, package, tool, size_bytes}).
  restore  : copy checkpoint 'id' back over the original and reload the package. Refuses over unsaved in-memory edits unless force=true.
  prune    : delete beyond an age/size budget.
  status   : capture mode, storage dir, entry count, total size.
  help     : full documentation.

TYPICAL RECOVERY:
  1. action='list', package_filter='BP_Player'
  2. action='restore', id='<from list>'

Capture is automatic and passive; this tool never creates checkpoints itself. The first save of a brand-new asset records nothing (no previous version exists).

action.description: Operation: list, restore, prune, status, help

package_filter.description: [list] Case-insensitive substring matched against the package path

force.description: [restore] Discard unsaved in-memory edits on the target package (default false)

max_total_mb.description: [prune] Keep total storage under this many megabytes (default 1024)

name: lookup_class
description:
Reflect a UClass straight from native C++: inheritance chain, UPROPERTY list with types/specifiers/tooltips, UFUNCTION signatures with Blueprint exposure - the answer to 'what can I actually call or set on this class'. Complements discover_python_class (which shows the Python-binding surface; this shows the C++ truth, including members the bindings hide).

INPUT FORMS: 'AActor' (prefixed), 'Actor' (bare - prefix-verified, ambiguity is an error, never a guess), '/Script/Engine.Actor' (exact), '/Game/BP_Thing.BP_Thing_C' (loaded Blueprint class).

DEFAULTS: own members only (include_inherited=false; the inheritance_chain tells you where to look next), tooltips on, 100 members per list.

TYPICAL USES:
  - before writing C++/Python against an unfamiliar class
  - resolving 'does this property exist and is it BlueprintReadWrite?'
  - member_filter='Health' to find everything health-related on a class

class_name.description: Class to reflect: 'AActor', 'Actor', '/Script/Engine.Actor' or a loaded Blueprint generated class path

include_inherited.description: Include members from super classes (default false)

member_filter.description: Case-insensitive substring filter applied to property and function names

max_members.description: Cap per list (default 100, max 1000); totals are always reported

name: deep_research
description: Web research and GPS geocoding — no API key required. Use 'search' to look up any topic via DuckDuckGo and get real web results with titles, URLs, and snippets. Use 'fetch_page' to read the full content of any URL as clean markdown (great for Unreal Engine documentation, Dev Community posts, API references). Use 'geocode' to convert any place name or address into GPS coordinates (lat/lng) for use with the terrain_data tool. Use 'reverse_geocode' to convert GPS coordinates back into a human-readable place name. Typical deep research workflow: search → fetch_page on the best URL → synthesize. Typical terrain workflow: geocode 'Mount Fuji' → pass lat/lng to terrain_data.

query.description: For search: topic or question. For geocode: place name or address (e.g. 'Mount Fuji', 'Grand Canyon South Rim').

url.description: For fetch_page: the full URL to fetch and convert to markdown (e.g. https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/...).

name: get_editor_context
description:
One read-only snapshot of what the user is looking at RIGHT NOW: loaded level, play session state, the most recently activated asset editor (active_asset), all open asset editors, the Content Browser selection, the actors selected in the viewport, and the Blueprint graph nodes selected in an open Blueprint editor.

Call this FIRST whenever a request says 'this blueprint', 'the selected actors', 'here', 'what I have open' - it resolves deixis into concrete asset paths you can feed to read_blueprint, manage_level_actors and friends.

RESULT SHAPE:
  level {name, path, dirty} | play_session: stopped|playing|simulating
  active_asset {name, class, path}       <- most recently activated editor tab
  open_assets[] / content_browser_selection[] {name, class, path} (+ *_total)
  selected_actors[] {label, class, location{x,y,z}} (+ selected_actors_total)
  selected_blueprint_nodes[] {title, type, node_id} (+ *_total)
  summary: one human-readable line

Selection lives only in the open editor UI - nothing here loads, modifies or saves any asset.

max_items.description: Cap per list (open assets, selections, nodes). Default 25, max 200

name: read_logs
description: Read and filter Unreal Engine log files. Actions: list (browse logs), info (file details), read (paginated content), tail (last N lines), head (first N lines), filter (regex search), errors (find errors), warnings (find warnings), since (new content since line), help (documentation). File aliases: main/system (project log), chat/revvy (chat log), llm (raw API log).

action.description: Operation: list, info, read, tail, head, filter, errors, warnings, since, help

file.description: Log file path or alias (main, chat, llm). Required for most actions.

category.description: [list] Filter by category: System, Blueprint, Niagara, Revvy

last_line.description: [since] Last line number you read (for getting new content)

name: pie_control
description:
Start, stop and inspect Play In Editor sessions - run the game inside the editor to verify gameplay changes actually behave, then stop and keep editing.

Transitions are DEFERRED: the engine performs the start/stop on a following frame, so both return {requested: true}; confirm with action='status'.

ACTIONS:
  start   : play the current level (or 'map' override) in the active viewport. simulate=true to simulate without possessing a player.
  stop    : end the active session.
  status  : stopped | playing | simulating, plus map, play_time_seconds, num_player_controllers, is_paused.
  help    : full documentation.

TYPICAL LOOP:
  1. edit gameplay code / Blueprints
  2. action='start'
  3. action='status'  (confirm playing; optionally capture_from_pose to look at it)
  4. action='stop'  -> keep editing

Nothing is saved by PIE; unsaved level changes play as-is.

map.description: [start] Long package name of the map to play (e.g. /Game/Maps/MyLevel). Default: the currently loaded level

simulate.description: [start] true = Simulate In Editor (no player possession). Default false = Play In Editor

name: execute_python_code
description: Execute Python code in Unreal Engine. IMPORTANT: Use 'import unreal' (lowercase). For subsystems use: unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.LevelEditorSubsystem). Returns stdout, stderr, and execution status.

code.description: Python code to execute. Must start with 'import unreal' (lowercase). For editor subsystems use unreal.get_editor_subsystem()

name: discover_python_module
description: Discover contents of a Python module. IMPORTANT: The module name is 'unreal' (lowercase, not 'Unreal'). Use this before execute_python_code to find available classes/functions.

module_name.description: Name of the Python module. Use 'unreal' (lowercase) for Unreal Engine APIs

name_filter.description: Filter results by name substring (case-insensitive). E.g. 'Blueprint' to find Blueprint-related items

max_items.description: Maximum items to return (default 100, 0 = unlimited). Use lower values to prevent context blowout

name: discover_python_class
description: Discover methods and attributes of a Python class with optional filtering.

class_name.description: Fully qualified class name, or a comma-separated list to discover several classes in one call (e.g. 'unreal.BlueprintService, unreal.MaterialService')

method_filter.description: Filter methods by name substring (case-insensitive). '|' ORs keywords: 'create|delete|compile' matches any of them

max_methods.description: Maximum methods to return (default 0 = no explicit cap). Large classes are still bounded by a response budget: docstrings are shortened first, then trailing methods are held back, and the reply says so via docstrings_trimmed/truncated

include_inherited.description: Include inherited methods (default false). Set true for all methods including base class

include_private.description: Include private methods starting with _ (default false)

name: discover_python_function
description: Get signature and documentation for a Python function.

function_name.description: Fully qualified function name (e.g. 'unreal.load_asset'). Alias: function_path

name: list_python_subsystems
description: List all Unreal Engine editor subsystems. Access via: unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.SubsystemName). Example: subsys = unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.LevelEditorSubsystem)

name: manage_skills
description: Discover and load domain-specific knowledge skills (workflows, gotchas, property formats). Skills are organized as an INDEX (SKILL.md — concise workflows + gotchas) plus optional SUB-DOCS (siblings — deeper reference material loaded on demand). Actions: 'list' — return every skill with its description, classes, engine bucket, and a `sections` array naming each loadable sub-doc. Call this once to discover what's available without loading content. 'suggest' — keyword search across skill names/descriptions/keywords. Use when you know the domain but not the skill name. 'load' — load a skill's index (just `SKILL.md`) OR a specific sub-doc. Use `skill_name='<skill>'` for the index, `skill_name='<skill>/<section>'` for a sub-doc (e.g. 'state-trees/transitions'). The response includes `available_sections` so you can decide whether you need to load any sub-doc. Use `skill_names` (array) to batch-load multiple in one call with deduplicated class lists.

query.description: Query string to match against skill keywords (for 'suggest' action)

skill_name.description: Skill to load (for 'load' action). Accepts: directory name (e.g. 'state-trees'), `name`/`display_name` field from frontmatter, or a sub-doc path like 'state-trees/transitions' to load only that sibling .md file. An optional engine qualifier prefix (e.g. 'unreal/state-trees', 'shared/revvy', 'godot/unity-overview') scopes the lookup to that engine bucket; bare names check the active engine bucket first, then 'shared'. Index loads (no slash) return just SKILL.md; sub-doc loads return only the requested file. Class metadata (revvy_classes/unreal_classes) always comes from the index.

skill_names.description: Array of skills to load together (for 'load' action). Each entry follows the same syntax as `skill_name`. Use this when you need several related skills in one call.

name: terrain_data
description: Generate heightmaps, map images, and water feature data from real-world terrain. Requires an active Revvy API key. Actions: generate_heightmap, preview_elevation, get_map_image, list_styles, get_water_features. IMPORTANT: Use the 'resolution' parameter to match your landscape resolution. Heightmap workflow: 1) preview_elevation for suggested settings (returns suggestedZScale, suggestedXYScales by resolution). 2) generate_heightmap with resolution matching your landscape. 3) Import via ULandscapeService.import_heightmap() (auto-creates a matching landscape if missing, but explicit create_landscape is recommended for real-world XY/Z scale control). CRITICAL: Use suggestedXYScales[resolution] as the landscape X and Y scale — do NOT use the default 100. Water workflow (after heightmap is imported): 1) get_water_features with the same lng/lat/map_size — saves JSON to Saved/Terrain/ and returns a summary with the file path. 2) Read the saved JSON file: json_str = open(file_path).read() 3) Water bodies use 'ue5_rings', waterways use 'ue5_points'. Both are origin-centered.

action.description: Action: generate_heightmap | preview_elevation | get_map_image | list_styles | get_water_features

lng.description: Longitude of center point (e.g. -122.4194 for San Francisco)

lat.description: Latitude of center point (e.g. 37.7749 for San Francisco)

map_size.description: Map size in km (default 17.28). Use the same value for heightmap and get_water_features.

format.description: Output format for generate_heightmap: png (default), raw, zip

resolution.description: Output resolution NxN pixels for generate_heightmap. MUST match landscape resolution. Use ULandscapeService.calculate_landscape_resolution() to compute. Common: 505 (8x8,63,1), 1009 (8x8,63,2 or 16x16,63,1), 1017 (8x8,127,1). Default: 1009

base_level.description: Base elevation offset in meters (default 0; use preview_elevation for good value)

height_scale.description: Height scale percentage 1-250 (default 100; use preview_elevation for good value)

water_depth.description: Water depth in Cities: Skylines units (default 40)

gravity_center.description: Water flow direction 0-13: 0=disabled, 1=center, 2=N, 3=NE, 4=E, 5=SE, 6=S, 7=SW, 8=W, 9=NW, 10=north side, 11=east side, 12=south side, 13=west side

plains_height.description: Height threshold for plains smoothing in meters (default 140)

style.description: Map image style for get_map_image: satellite-v9, outdoors-v11, streets-v11, light-v10, dark-v10

save_path.description: File path to save output. Default: <ProjectDir>/Saved/Terrain/
